data.title: The Letter Never Sent
data.excerpt: Some things are easier to write than to say, especially to someone who can no longer answer.
content: The letter had been sitting inside the drawer for eleven years.
It was written on a quiet Sunday afternoon, when Daniel still believed there would always be another chance to say what mattered.
I don't know if I should send this. Maybe I am writing it only because saying these things out loud has always been harder.
I should have stayed that evening.
I should have answered your last question instead of pretending I didn't hear it.
The letter continued for four pages.
Years later, while cleaning the house, he found the envelope again. The paper had turned yellow around the edges.
He read the letter from beginning to end.
Not because the words no longer hurt, but because they finally belonged to the past.
He folded the letter carefully and placed it back in the drawer.
Some things did not need to be sent to become goodbyes.
